The image description should be detailed to ensure the resulting image matches the desired subject and surroundings; otherwise, these aspects will be chosen randomly. This function is not intended for generating images from textual data. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

desc.description: A single string that provides a detailed description of the desired image. For example, 'a sunset over the mountains with a lake in the foreground'.

file_name.description: The name of the file to which the generated image will be saved. It should include the file extension, such as 'image.png'.

function.description: Converts the provided text content to speech and saves the resulting audio to a file. This function is intended for voice narration and should be used accordingly. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The Markdown formatted text content to be written to the file.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the Markdown content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

content.description: The HTML content to be written to the file. Must contain valid HTML structure.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the HTML content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

function.description: Executes a search query using the DuckDuckGo search engine and returns a specified number of search results from a given source. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

query.description: The search term or phrase to be queried.

num_results.description: The maximum number of search results to return. A positive integer.

source.description: The source from which the search results should be fetched.

function.name: get_url_content
function.description: Scrapes the specified URL for textual data and returns the content as a string. This function is useful for extracting information from web pages when a URL is provided. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The web address of the page to scrape. It should be a valid URL format, such as 'http://www.example.com'.

timeout.description: The maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, with a default value that allows for a reasonable amount of time for most web pages to load.

user_agent.description: The User-Agent string to be used for the HTTP request to simulate a particular browser, which is optional. Some websites may require this for access.

message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run** example that creates a new Compute Engine VM on Google Cloud Platform (GCP) with:

| Requirement | How it’s satisfied |
|-------------|--------------------|
| **GPU** | NVIDIA RTX A6000 (the only GPU type that supports the RTX A6000) |
| **OS** | Ubuntu 20.04 LTS |
| **Machine type** | `n1-standard-8` (8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM – enough headroom for the GPU) |
| **Zone** | `us-central1-a` (you can change this to any zone that offers GPUs) |
| **Project** | Replace `<YOUR_PROJECT_ID>` with your actual GCP project ID |

---

## 1️⃣ Using the `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# 1. Authenticate (if you haven’t already)
gcloud auth login

# 2. Set your project
gcloud config set project <YOUR_PROJECT_ID>

# 3. Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create my-rtx-a6000 \
    --zone=us-central1-a \
    --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \
    --subnet=default \
    --network-tier=PREMIUM \
    --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
    --provisioning-model=STANDARD \
    --service-account=<YOUR_SERVICE_ACCOUNT>@<YOUR_PROJECT_ID>.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
    --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
    --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
    --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
    --boot-disk-size=100GB \
    --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
    --boot-disk-device-name=my-rtx-a6000 \
    --no-shielded-secure-boot \
    --no-shielded-vtpm \
    --no-shielded-integrity-monitoring \
    --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \
    --accelerator=count=1,type=nvidia-tesla-a6000 \
    --reservation-affinity=any
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--zone` | Where the VM will live. |
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM allocation. |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Pulls the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image. |
| `--boot-disk-size` | SSD size (adjust if you need more storage). |
| `--accelerator` | Adds one RTX A6000 GPU. |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script` | Optional: runs a script at boot (e.g., installs CUDA drivers). |

> **Tip:** If you don’t have a service account yet, you can omit the `--service-account` line and let GCP use the default compute service account.

---

## 2️⃣ Using the REST API (JSON)

If you prefer to call the API directly (e.g., from a script or Terraform), here’s the exact JSON payload you’d POST to `https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/<YOUR_PROJECT_ID>/zones/us-central1-a/instances`.

```json
{
  "name": "my-rtx-a6000",
  "machineType": "projects/<YOUR_PROJECT_ID>/zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/<YOUR_PROJECT_ID>/zones/us-central1-a/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "<YOUR_SERVICE_ACCOUNT>@<YOUR_PROJECT_ID>.iam.gserviceaccount.com",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/<YOUR_PROJECT_ID>/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "reservationAffinity": { "consumeReservationType": "ANY_RESERVATION" },
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y cuda-drivers"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

### How to POST this JSON

```bash
curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/<YOUR_PROJECT_ID>/zones/us-central1-a/instances"
```

Replace `@instance.json` with the path to a file containing the JSON above.

---

## 3️⃣ Quick Checklist

- [ ] **Project ID** – replace `<YOUR_PROJECT_ID>` everywhere.
- [ ] **Service Account** – ensure it has the `Compute Admin` role (or equivalent).
- [ ] **GPU Availability** – check that the zone you choose actually offers RTX A6000 GPUs (`gcloud compute accelerator-types list --filter="name:nvidia-tesla-a6000" --format="table(name,zone)"`).
- [ ] **Billing** – make sure billing is enabled for the project; GPU instances incur extra charges.
- [ ] **Startup Script** – optional but recommended to install CUDA drivers automatically.

Once you run either the `gcloud` command or the REST POST, GCP will provision the VM. You can then SSH into it:

```bash
gcloud compute ssh my-rtx-a6000 --zone=us-central1-a
```

Enjoy your RTX A6000-powered Ubuntu 20.04 instance!
